notes: Use Jinshu031’s explicit Hui-empress Jia name Nanfeng as the bridge between chapter053’s named Jia empress and chapters028/032. Preserve every already-merged member; independently review all primary supplied contexts. The rejected two-record proposal remains held rather than relabeling its nickname as strong evidence.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 及楊駿居內府，以戟為衛，死時又為戟所害傷。

translations.literal: When Yang Jun dwelt in the inner palace he used halberds for guards; at death he was again wounded by halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jun's halberd corps foretold his own skewering.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 楊後被廢，賈后絕其膳八日而崩，葬街郵亭北，百姓哀之也。

translations.literal: Empress Yang was deposed; Empress Jia starved her eight days until she died; she was buried north of Jieyou post; the people pitied her.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Yang died of Jia Nanfeng's hunger strike and was dumped by the courier station.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 雨火，武帝諱，蘭，楊後字也。

translations.literal: "Two fires" is Emperor Wu's taboo graph; "orchid" was Empress Yang's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators read the paired "fire" graphs as alluding to Emperor Wu's taboo name and "orchid" as Empress Yang Zhi's style name.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 又曰：「城東馬子莫嚨哅，此至來年纏女閤。」

translations.literal: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."
translations.idiomatic: It also said: "East-city colt, don't whinny — by next year you'll tangle in women's boudoirs."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 南風，賈后字也。

translations.literal: South wind" is Empress Jia's style name.
translations.idiomatic: Nanfeng was the empress's sobriquet.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 白，晉行也。

translations.literal: "White" is Jin's phase color.
translations.idiomatic: White stood for metal — Jin's element.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 魯，賈謐國也。

translations.literal: "Lu" is Jia Mi's princedom.
translations.idiomatic: Lu mapped onto Jia Mi's noble seat.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 言賈后將與謐為亂，以危太子，而趙王因釁咀嚼豪賢，以成篡奪，不得其死之應也。

translations.literal: It means Empress Jia would riot with Mi to endanger the heir, while Prince Zhao would chew up great men and seize the throne — an omen of dying badly.
translations.idiomatic: The gloss tied the verses to Jia's coup plot and Sima Lun's coming slaughter.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 元康中，天下商農通著大鄣日。

translations.literal: In Yuankang merchants and farmers all wore wide sun-hats.
translations.idiomatic: Yuankang fashion made everyone don huge visors.

currentSummary.descriptor: Consort (empress of Emperor Hui; de facto ruler, deposed and killed 300)

compactPerson: Consort (empress of Emperor Hui; de facto ruler, deposed and killed 300)

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 時人方知謀出於穆，非玫之意。

translations.literal: People then learned the plot came from Mu—not Mei’s intent.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did folk realize Zhou Mu schemed it—not Mei.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 惠賈皇后

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Emperor Hui
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia of Emperor Hui

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 惠賈皇后諱南風，平陽人也，小名時。

translations.literal: Empress Jia of Hui, taboo Nanfeng, native of Pingyang, childhood name Shi.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia Nanfeng of Pingyang—pet name Shi.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 父充，別有傳。

translations.literal: Her father Chong has separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Her father Jia Chong has his own biography.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 始欲聘后妹午，午年十二，小太子一歲，短小未勝衣。

translations.literal: At first they wished to engage younger sister Wu—Wu twelve years old, one year younger than crown prince, too short for robes.
translations.idiomatic: They first chose sister Wu—twelve, petite beside the heir.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 更娶南風，時年十五，大太子二歲。

translations.literal: They switched to Nanfeng—then fifteen, two years elder than crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: They wed Nanfeng instead—fifteen, two years his senior.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 泰始八年二月辛卯[7]，冊拜太子妃。

translations.literal: Eighth Taishi year second month xinmao [7]—invested crown princess.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinmao day of the second month of 272 she became crown princess [7].

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 妒忌多權詐，太子畏而惑之，嬪御罕有進幸者。

translations.literal: Jealous, crafty in intrigue—crown prince feared yet dazed—concubines rarely gained favor.
translations.idiomatic: Jealous and scheming, she cowed the befuddled prince—other women seldom touched him.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 盡召東宮大小官屬，為設宴會，而密封疑事，使太子決之，停信待反。

translations.literal: He summoned all eastern palace officials large and small, set banquet, sealed doubtful affairs ordering crown prince to decide—stopped courier awaiting reply.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted Eastern Palace staff, sealed riddling cases for the heir to solve.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 妃大懼，倩外人作答。

translations.literal: Consort greatly frightened—begged outsider compose answers.
translations.idiomatic: Princess Jia panicked and outsourced answers.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 答者多引古義。

translations.literal: Answerers mostly cited classical meanings.
translations.idiomatic: Ghostwriters packed classics.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 不如直以意對。」

translations.literal: Better answer straight from plain intent.”
translations.idiomatic: Plain speech fits better."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 妃大喜，語泓：「便為我好答，富貴與汝共之。」

translations.literal: Consort rejoiced, telling Hong: "Answer well for me—wealth and honor shared with you."
translations.idiomatic: She thrilled: "Write plainly for me—wealth and honor we will share."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 泓素有小才，具草，令太子自寫。

translations.literal: Hong always had small talent—drafted fully—ordered crown prince himself copy.
translations.idiomatic: Hong drafted; she made the prince copy.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 先示太子少傅衛瓘，瓘大踧踖，眾人乃知瓘先有毀言，殿上皆稱萬歲。

translations.literal: First showed Junior Mentor Wei Guan—Guan greatly ashamed—all knew Guan earlier had slanderous words—hall cheered ten thousand years.
translations.idiomatic: He flashed it at Wei Guan—Wei squirmed; courtiers jeered Guan’s prior slanders.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 充密遣語妃云：「衛瓘老奴，幾破汝家。」

translations.literal: Chong secretly sent word to consort: "Old slave Wei Guan nearly ruined your house."
translations.idiomatic: Jia Chong whispered to the consort, "Old slave Wei Guan nearly ruined your house."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 妃性酷虐，嘗手殺數人。

translations.literal: Consort nature cruel—often personally killed several persons.
translations.idiomatic: She killed with her own hands.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 或以戟擲孕妾，子隨刃墮地。

translations.literal: Sometimes threw halberd at pregnant concubine—child fell with blade to ground.
translations.idiomatic: She hurled a ji at a pregnant girl—the infant fell with the blow.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 帝聞之，大怒，已修金墉城，將廢之。

translations.literal: Emperor hearing greatly furious—already repaired Metal-Walled Fortress—about to depose her.
translations.idiomatic: Wu rebuilt Jinyong cage ready to depose her.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 充華趙粲從容言曰：「賈妃年少，妒是婦人之情耳，長自當差。

translations.literal: Honorable Lady Zhao Can calmly said: “Consort Jia still young—jealousy is woman’s feeling—long maturity will correct.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Can soothed him: “She’s young—jealousy passes.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 願陛下察之。」

translations.literal: May Your Majesty investigate.”
translations.idiomatic: May Your Majesty weigh this carefully."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 惠帝即位，立為皇后，生河東、臨海、始平公主、哀獻皇女。

translations.literal: When Emperor Hui ascended—established empress—bore Hedong, Linhai, Shiping princesses and mournful imperial daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Hui made her queen—mother of Hedong, Linhai, Shiping princesses and others.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后暴戾日甚。

translations.literal: Consort violent cruelty daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Her cruelty mounted daily.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 侍中賈模，后之族兄，右衛郭彰，后之從舅，並以才望居位，與楚王瑋、東安公繇分掌朝政。

translations.literal: Palace Attendant Jia Mo—consort’s lineage elder; Guards-general Guo Zhang—consort’s maternal uncle—both by talent and prestige held posts sharing governance with Prince Chu Wei and Duke Dongan Yao.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo and Guo Zhang ran court beside Sima Wei and Sima Yao.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后母廣城君養孫賈謐干預國事，權侔人主。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng raised grandson Jia Mi meddling state affairs—authority matched sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo raised Jia Mi—his power rivaled the throne.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 繇密欲廢后，賈氏憚之。

translations.literal: Yao secretly wished depose consort—Jia faction feared him.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Yao plotted deposition—Jias feared him.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 及太宰亮、衛瓘等表繇徙帶方，奪楚王中候，后知瑋怨之，乃使帝作密詔令瑋誅瓘、亮，以報宿憾。

translations.literal: When Grand Mentor Liang and Wei Guan memorialized to exile Yao to Daifang and strip Prince Chu of central army inspector—consort knew Wei bore grudge—had emperor forge secret edict ordering Wei to kill Guan and Liang—settling old hatred.
translations.idiomatic: When Sima Liang and Wei Guan banished Yao and clipped Wei’s guard—she forged orders for Sima Wei to murder Liang and Wei.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 模知后凶暴，恐禍及己，乃與裴頠、王衍謀廢之，衍悔而謀寢。

translations.literal: Mo knew the consort was fierce—feared disaster reaching himself—and with Pei Wei and Wang Yan plotted her deposition—Yan repented—the plot slept.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mo saw danger—plotted with Pei Wei and Wang Yan to depose her—Wang Yan backed out.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后遂荒淫放恣，與太醫令程據等亂彰內外。

translations.literal: Consort then wanton and dissolute—with Imperial Physician Cheng Ju and others licentious noise inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: She ran riot with physician Cheng Ju.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 洛南有盜尉部小吏，端麗美容止，既給冢役，忽有非常衣服，眾咸疑其竊盜，尉嫌而辯之。

translations.literal: South of Luo petty clerk of thief corps—handsome bearing—assigned tomb labor yet wore extraordinary clothes—all suspected theft—captain interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: A pretty clerk toiling tombs wore silk—suspected theft.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 賈后疏親欲求盜物，往聽對辭。

translations.literal: Consort distant kin sought stolen goods—went to hear interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: Jia kin listened to his confession.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 小吏云：「先行逢一老嫗，說家有疾病，師卜云宜得城南少年厭之，欲暫相煩，必有重報。

translations.literal: Petty clerk said: “Going ahead met old woman saying household illness—diviners said need youth south of wall to suppress—wished borrow briefly—promised rich reward.
translations.idiomatic: The clerk said, "Going ahead I met an old woman who said her household was ill; diviners said a youth from south of the city should suppress it, and she wished briefly to trouble me, promising rich reward.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 見留數夕，共寢歡宴，臨出贈此眾物。」

translations.literal: Detained several nights—slept together feasting—departing gifted many goods.”
translations.idiomatic: She kept me several nights—we feasted and slept together—and as I left she gave me all these goods."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 聽者聞其形狀，知是賈后，慚笑而去，尉亦解意。

translations.literal: Hearers hearing shape knew it was Empress Jia—left ashamed laughing—captain understood.
translations.idiomatic: Listeners recognized Jia Nanfeng—the captain dropped charges.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 時他人入者多死，惟此小吏，以后愛之，得全而出。

translations.literal: Others entering mostly died—only this petty clerk—because consort loved him—escaped whole.
translations.idiomatic: Others died visiting her bed—only her pet survived.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 遂謀廢太子，以所養代立。

translations.literal: Then plotted depose crown prince—establish fosterling.
translations.idiomatic: She meant to replace the heir with him.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 時洛中謠曰：「南風烈烈吹黃沙，遙望魯國鬱嵯峨，前至三月滅汝家。」

translations.literal: Then Luoyang rhyme said: "South wind fierce blows yellow sand—far gaze Lu kingdom towering—before third month ends your house."
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang sang: "Nanfeng blasts yellow dust—far off Lu towers loom—by the third moon your house will fall."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后母廣城君以后無子，甚敬重愍懷，每勸厲后，使加慈愛。

translations.literal: Consort mother Lady Guangcheng because consort lacked sons greatly revered Crown Prince Minhuai—often urged consort—made her add kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Guo prized Minhuai—begged Jia to cherish him.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 賈謐恃貴驕縱，不能推崇太子，廣城君恒切責之。

translations.literal: Jia Mi relied on pride—could not honor crown prince—Lady Guangcheng constantly scolded.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Mi insulted the heir—Lady Guo scolded him.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后出侍疾十餘日，太子常往宜城第，將醫出入，恂恂盡禮。

translations.literal: The empress went out to tend her mother during her illness for more than ten days. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence, bringing physicians in and out and respectfully observing every propriety.
translations.idiomatic: The empress spent more than ten days away tending her sick mother. The crown prince often visited the Yicheng residence with physicians, behaving respectfully and observing every courtesy.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 宜城臨終執后手，令盡意于太子，言甚切至。

translations.literal: Yicheng dying grasped consort’s hand—ordered exhaust feeling toward crown prince—speech extremely earnest.
translations.idiomatic: She clasped Jia’s hand—beg her shield Minhuai.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 又曰：「趙粲及午必亂汝事，我死後，勿復聽入，深憶吾言。」

translations.literal: Also said: “Zhao Can and Wu surely ruin your affairs—after I die—never hear them again—deeply remember my words.”
translations.idiomatic: She also said, "Zhao Can and Jia Wu will surely disrupt your affairs; after I die, do not admit them again—remember my words well."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后不能遵之，遂專制天下，威服內外。

translations.literal: Consort could not obey—thereupon monopolized realm—awe subdued inner and outer.
translations.idiomatic: Jia ignored—ruled alone.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 更與粲、午專為姦謀，誣害太子，眾惡彰著。

translations.literal: Further with Can, Wu solely plotted wickedness—slandered harmed crown prince—crowds of evils manifest.
translations.idiomatic: She schemed with them against Minhuai.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后曰：「詔當從我出，何詔也？」

translations.literal: Consort said: "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"
translations.idiomatic: She snapped, "Edicts issue from me—what edict is this?"

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 后至上閤，遙呼帝曰：「陛下有婦，使人廢之，亦行自廢。」

translations.literal: Consort reaching upper chamber cried distant emperor: “Your Majesty has wife yet lets others depose her—you yourself will be deposed.”
translations.idiomatic: Reaching the upper chamber she cried to the emperor, "Your Majesty has a wife, yet you let others depose her—you will be deposed yourself."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 又問冏曰：「起事者誰？」

translations.literal: Again asked Jiong: “Who raised revolt?”
translations.idiomatic: She asked Jiong again, "Who raised this affair?"

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 惠皇稟質，王縱其嚚，識暗鳴蛙，智昏文蛤。

translations.literal: Emperor Hui received substance; consorts of Wang indulged their viciousness; insight dark as croaking frogs; wisdom dim as patterned clams.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hui was dull by nature while the Wang women unleashed their malice—his wit was no brighter than a frog's croak, his judgment no sharper than a clam in mud.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 南風肆狡，扇禍稽天。

translations.literal: South Wind wantonly cunning; fanning calamity reaching Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Nanfeng gave free rein to cunning and fanned disaster until it scraped the sky.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 初踐椒宮，逞梟心于長樂；

translations.literal: First treading the pepper palace; displaying owl heart in Changle;
translations.idiomatic: Once she mounted to the pepper-scented halls she showed an owl's heart in Changle Palace;

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 二楊繼寵，福極災生。

translations.literal: Two Yangs succeeded favor; fortune extreme calamity born.
translations.idiomatic: Two Yang women rode successive favor—fortune peaked and disaster followed.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 南風熾虐，國喪身傾。

translations.literal: South Wind blazing cruelty; state lost body overturned.
translations.idiomatic: South Wind burned fierce and cruel—the realm fell and she herself was cast down.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 獻容幸亂，居辱疑榮。

translations.literal: Xianrong favored turmoil; dwelling in shame suspected glory.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Xianrong throve on chaos and wore infamy as if it were honor.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 及長，不好學，惟與左右嬉戲，不能尊敬保傅。

translations.literal: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.
translations.idiomatic: When grown he cared nothing for study and only played games with attendants; he could not honor tutors or guardians.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 賈后素忌太子有令譽，因此密敕黃門閹宦媚諛于太子曰：「殿下誠可及壯時極意所欲，何為恆自拘束？」

translations.literal: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia had long envied the crown prince's fine reputation and therefore secretly ordered Yellow Gate eunuchs to flatter him: 'Your Highness may indeed indulge every whim while still young—why bind yourself so tightly?'

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 每見喜怒之際，輒歎曰：「殿下不知用威刑，天下豈得畏服！」

translations.literal: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they saw him pleased or angry, they would sigh: "Your Highness does not know how to use authority and punishments. How could the realm fear and obey you?"

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 九年六月，有桑生於宮西廂，日長尺餘，數日而枯。

translations.literal: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the west wing of the palace; it grew more than a chi each day and withered after several days.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth lunar month of the ninth year, a mulberry sprouted in the palace’s west wing. It grew more than a chi each day, then withered after several days.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 十二月，賈后將廢太子，詐稱上不和，呼太子入朝。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, when Empress Jia would depose the crown prince, she falsely claimed the emperor was unwell and summoned the crown prince to court.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 既至，後不見，置於別室，遣婢陳舞賜以酒棗，逼飲醉之。

translations.literal: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived she did not receive him but lodged him in a side chamber, sent maid Chen Wu with ale and jujubes, and forced him drunk.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 遍示諸公王，莫有言者，惟張華、裴頠證明太子。

translations.literal: No one among lords and dukes spoke except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei who verified the crown prince's innocence.
translations.idiomatic: It was shown all around to the lords and princes; none spoke, except Zhang Hua and Pei Wei, who verified the crown prince's innocence.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 賈后使董猛矯以長廣公主辭白帝曰：「事宜速決，而群臣各有不同，若有不從詔，宜以軍法從事。」

translations.literal: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: 'Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law.'
translations.idiomatic: Empress Jia had Dong Meng falsely relay Princess Changguang's words to the emperor: "Matters must be settled quickly while ministers disagree—whoever disobeys the edict should face military law."

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 議至日西不決。

translations.literal: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.
translations.idiomatic: Deliberation lasted until sunset unresolved.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 又曰：「南風起兮吹白沙，遙望魯國郁嵯峨，千歲髑髏生齒牙。」

translations.literal: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'
translations.idiomatic: Another went: 'South wind rises blowing white sand; far off Lu kingdom gloomy and tall; thousand-year skulls sprout teeth.'

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 南風，后名；

translations.literal: 'South Wind' was the empress's name.
translations.idiomatic: 'South Wind' was the empress's name.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 沙門，太子小字也。

translations.literal: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.
translations.idiomatic: 'Shamen' was the crown prince's childhood byname.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 詔以廣陵王禮葬之。

translations.literal: An edict buried him with rites due Prince of Guangling.
translations.idiomatic: An edict buried him with rites due the Prince of Guangling.

fullPrimaryNameClaimUnitsAndAdjacentCont.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！

translations.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
